svg.aria-label: How the 128, 32 or 4 work items of a decode step are laid out on the 8 x 8 core grid
svg.title: How the 128, 32 or 4 work items of a decode step are laid out on the 8 x 8 core grid
svg.text: Work layout on one chip (Llama-3.1-8B, TP = 2: 4 KV heads and 16 query heads per chip)
each core does half the chunks; 1 merge round
each core does 1/16 of the chunks; 4 merge rounds
cores per item = min(64, max_cores_per_head x B x n_kv) / B / n_kv; heads per core = ceil(n_kv / (64 / B)).
Label: b<batch> for the batch row at 32; at 8 the digit is the KV head and 'r' marks the reducer (root) core of each pair; at 1 the shade is the KV head.
Chunks are dealt backwards: the root core (core_num 0) owns the LAST chunks, where the causal mask lands; core N-1 owns the first.
Fig. B2. The same kernel binary runs on every core; per-core runtime arguments say which (batch, head) item, which slice of chunks, and which tree role it has.
